notes: Yellow signs in stations. Big stations number the exits (A1, B3) or name them 東口, 西口.

examples.tl: 出口はどこですか。

notes: On doors, car parks and one-way gates, often paired with 出口 on the other door.

examples.tl: 入口はあちらです。
examples.en: The entrance is over that way.

notes: On door plates and buttons, often just 押. Polite form: 押します (oshimasu).

examples.tl: ドアを押してください。

notes: On door handles, often just 引. Polite form: 引きます (hikimasu). 自動 (jidō) = automatic door.

examples.tl: このドアは引いてください。

notes: On a board or curtain at restaurant and shop doors. 〜中 (chū) = in the middle of.

examples.tl: あの店は営業中です。

notes: Literally 'getting ready': closed between lunch and dinner or before opening. Come back later.

examples.tl: すみません、まだ準備中です。
examples.en: Sorry, we are not open yet.

notes: Opposite: 喫煙 (kitsuen) smoking; 喫煙所 = smoking area. Smoking on the street is banned in much of Tokyo.

examples.tl: この店は全席禁煙です。
examples.rom: Kono mise wa zenseki kin'en desu.

notes: The polite sign word. Department stores write 化粧室 (keshōshitsu); elsewhere トイレ or WC.

examples.tl: お手洗いは二階です。
examples.en: The restroom is on the second floor.

notes: On toilet and bath doors, usually in blue. At a hot spring the curtain reads 男湯 (otokoyu), men's bath.

examples.tl: 男湯はどちらですか。
examples.en: Which way is the men's bath?

notes: Usually in red. 女湯 (onnayu) = women's bath. Baths can swap sides overnight, so read the curtain each time.

examples.tl: こちらは女湯です。

notes: At restaurant doors and on train booking screens. 空席 (kūseki) = seats available.

examples.tl: すみません、ただいま満席です。
examples.en: Sorry, we are full at the moment.

notes: Lights up red as 売切 on vending and meal-ticket machines. 完売 (kanbai) means the same.

examples.tl: すみません、今日は売り切れです。
examples.en: Sorry, it is sold out today.

notes: The green running-man sign. 非常 (hijō) = emergency, as in 非常ボタン, the emergency button.

examples.tl: 非常口は廊下の奥にあります。
examples.rom: Hijōguchi wa rōka no oku ni arimasu.
examples.en: The emergency exit is at the end of the hallway.

notes: Elevator button that holds the doors, often with ◀▶ and labeled ひらく. Easy to mix up with 閉 (close).

examples.tl: 「開」ボタンを押してください。

notes: Elevator button ▶◀, often labeled しめる. On a shop door, 閉店 (heiten) = closed for the day.

examples.tl: 「閉」ボタンを押します。

notes: 〜禁止 (kinshi) = prohibited. 関係者以外立入禁止 = staff only. On trails it marks closed or dangerous paths.

examples.tl: ここは立入禁止です。

notes: Red or yellow signs at cliffs, rivers, building sites and electrical boxes.

examples.tl: この先は危険です。
examples.en: It is dangerous beyond this point.

notes: 足元注意 = watch your step, 頭上注意 = mind your head, 熊出没注意 = beware of bears.

examples.tl: 足元にご注意ください。

notes: Taped onto vending machines, ticket machines, toilets and escalators.

examples.tl: このエレベーターは故障中です。
examples.en: This elevator is out of order.

notes: The fixed day a shop closes each week. On the door: 定休日 水曜日 = closed Wednesdays.

examples.tl: 定休日は水曜日です。
examples.en: The regular closing day is Wednesday.

notes: 本日 (honjitsu) is the formal written 'today'. 臨時休業 (rinji kyūgyō) = unscheduled closure.

examples.tl: 入口に本日休業と書いてあります。
examples.rom: Iriguchi ni honjitsu kyūgyō to kaite arimasu.
examples.en: It says 'closed today' at the entrance.

notes: On departure boards and tickets: 3番線 (sanban-sen) = track 3.

examples.tl: 日光行きは5番線から出ます。
examples.rom: Nikkō yuki wa goban-sen kara demasu.
examples.en: The Nikko train leaves from track 5.

notes: Machine just inside the exit gates (のりこし精算): pay the difference if your ticket or IC balance falls short.

examples.tl: 精算機で足りない分を払ってください。
examples.rom: Seisanki de tarinai bun o haratte kudasai.
examples.en: Please pay the shortfall at the fare adjustment machine.

notes: Opposite: 有料 (yūryō) = paid. 入場無料 = free admission.

examples.tl: この地図は無料です。

notes: のみ = only, in written style. At small restaurants, shrines and rural buses. カード不可 = no cards.

examples.tl: すみません、お支払いは現金のみです。
examples.rom: Sumimasen, oshiharai wa genkin nomi desu.

notes: On price tags. 税抜 (zeinuki) or 税別 (zeibetsu) = before tax: add 10%, or 8% for takeout food.

examples.tl: この値段は税込ですか。
examples.rom: Kono nedan wa zeikomi desu ka.

notes: Common inside temple halls and museums. フラッシュ禁止 = no flash.

examples.tl: 中は撮影禁止です。

notes: 土足 = outdoor shoes. At temple halls, castle keeps, some inns and fitting rooms: use the shelf or bag provided.

examples.tl: ここから先は土足禁止です。
examples.rom: Koko kara saki wa dosoku kinshi desu.

notes: Seats at the car ends for elderly, pregnant or injured riders. You may sit, but give it up when needed.

examples.tl: ここは優先席です。

notes: Pink signs on the platform and windows, mostly in the morning rush. Men should board another car.

examples.tl: この車両は女性専用車です。
examples.rom: Kono sharyō wa josei sen'yōsha desu.

notes: On toilet panels with 大 (full) and 小 (light). 止 = stop the spray, おしり = rear wash. 呼出 calls staff: don't press.

examples.tl: トイレの水を流してください。
examples.rom: Toire no mizu o nagashite kudasai.

notes: On toilet locks, coin lockers and fitting rooms. 空き (aki) = vacant.

examples.tl: トイレは使用中です。
